messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for escalation PD#52341 — private control-plane connectivity failing for customer AcmeAnalytics (VPC: vpc-acme-prod). Auto-page to oncall.
pagerduty: Incident 52341 created — urgency: high. Trigger: control-plane-conn-failure (private). Runbook: /runbooks/private-controlplane-connectivity.md
maya_oncall: acked. I'll triage, pinging netops and infra. @kevin_sre you online? :wave:
kevin_sre: here. saw the page. quick checks: control-plane in our private region shows intermittent 504s to acme's VPC. healthchecks show agent heartbeat gaps ~30s.
support_emma: Acme reported timeouts for model deployments and webhooks failing to reach their control plane callbacks. Customer impact: deployment API errors and webhook retries. Customer ticket #ACME-882 opened.
maya_oncall: confirmed. Repro from our side: `curl -v https://private-control.acme.redwood-internal/health` -> sometimes hangs, sometimes 502.
kevin_sre: grabbing agent heartbeat logs from our agent pool in acme VPC.
kevin_sre: ssh'd into onprem-agent-03 (10.2.8.12). running `journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | tail -n 80`
kevin_sre: logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts and `connection reset by peer` entries every ~60s. Also kernel messages about NIC flaps.
netops_julie: seeing BGP withdraws from leaf-router in acme's region. Looks like their upstream provider is flapping a route to the private peering. I'm pulling route history.
netops_julie: `show bgp neighbors 10.0.0.1 flap-statistics` -> multiple flaps in last 10 minutes. Possibly noisy upstream.
infra_tom: on our side control plane pods look healthy but we have elevated 5xx from the control-plane ingress. Trying `kubectl logs -n redwood controlplane-ingress-1 --since=10m` now.
infra_tom: ingress logs show increased connection resets from IPs inside vpc-acme-prod. Could be packet loss or MTU mismatch on their side.
maya_oncall: summary: network instability between Acme's VPC and our private control plane causing agent heartbeats to drop and control-plane requests to intermittently fail. Impact: Acme cannot reliably create deployments and webhooks fail.
support_emma: told Acme we are investigating and suggested retry/backoff. They've asked for ETA.
maya_oncall: immediate mitigations:
- ask Acme to engage their cloud provider to stabilize BGP (netops already reached out)
- enable fallback to hosted control plane for Acme for non-sensitive workloads (will reduce latency but restore functionality)
- capture packet traces and upload to S3 for root cause analysis

kevin_sre: executed a temporary agent restart on onprem-agent-03: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent` — agent came back but heartbeat gaps persisted. So restart is only partial mitigation.
netops_julie: pushed a support ticket to Acme's ISP (ticket #ISP-998) with route flap evidence and next-hop changes. Asked them to check interface errors and physical link.
maya_oncall: enabling hosted fallback for Acme (opt-in) via feature flag on the customer record. Doing the switch now.
infra_tom: applied config change to route control-plane traffic for acme to hosted-control.redwood.ai (non-sensitive) — `PATCH /internal/customers/acme/routing { "fallback": "hosted" }`
infra_tom: applied. monitoring: p99 latency for acme after switch dropping to normal. Confirming with customer.
support_emma: Acme confirmed: webhook retries now succeed when targeted at hosted endpoint. They're able to create test deployments. They want full roll back once link stable.
maya_oncall: ticket updates: added timeline, logs, and actions. Attaching `journalctl` snippets and packet captures to ACME-882.
kevin_sre: captured `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/acme-flap-2026-06-12.pcap` and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/52341/acme-flap.pcap
maya_oncall: tagging this as partial mitigation. We restored customer functionality via hosted fallback. Root cause likely external BGP/flapping; NetOps leading external escalation.
netops_julie: continuing escalation with ISP. If they can't remediate, recommend Acme move peering to alternate provider or add redundant peer.
maya_oncall: Now doing on-call handoff. I'm wrapping up and handing to @kevin_sre for overnight follow-up and RCA doc. Key actions for overnight:
- monitor for further flaps and heartbeat gaps
- coordinate with Acme/SISP for BGP resolution
- prepare RCA draft with timestamps + pcaps

kevin_sre: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring and will file RCA. Assigning follow-ups:
- netops_julie: continue ISP escalation (owner)
- infra_tom: revert fallback once stable (owner)
- support_emma: communicate status to Acme and coordinate maintenance window

maya_oncall: thumbs up. leaving channel, oncall clear. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident 52341 status: acknowledged -> mitigated (partial) by fallback. Next step: RCA in 24h. PagerDuty: note state change.
pagerduty: Incident 52341 annotated: mitigated partial, assigned to kevin_sre for RCA. Escalation to SRE manager not required.
customer_acme_ops: thanks for the quick mitigation. We'll keep our ISP engaged and report back. Appreciate the hosted fallback option — saved our morning slate.
kevin_sre: creating post-incident doc now and will link to support ticket ACME-882. I'll include timeline, pcaps, and recommended network changes.
maya_oncall: handing off fully. Good job everyone. :clap:
